conviction_note: The H1 numbers and the FY27 guide were pre-released on 11 Sep, so the move sits in what the release adds: Ian Brown's first results as CEO (in post since 28 Sep), and a 'fuller update on the regulatory landscape and its implications' that the company promised on 9 Oct. That pushes the size up to ~6%, against a 3.1% vol proxy and +5.0% on both of the last two interim days. The sign is close to a coin flip. A reset by a new CEO against FY28 consensus (+4% NTS, +2.7% EBITDA, against UK headwinds the company says continue into H2) weighs against a 5% short that is building and two up-days on past interims. So p_up is 46 and the scaled number is -0.48. The findings sum to -1.9, which is larger because each negative is sized on its own inference while the positioning offset sits partly in p_up.

findings.finding: On 9 Oct Trainline committed to give 'a fuller update on the regulatory landscape and its implications' with these results. It had just said the ORR's draft GBR Retail Code 'require[s] further strengthening', so the release will carry a new regulatory section, most likely a cautious one, on an issue that has driven this stock's largest moves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GBR and state-retailer news has moved TRN hard. The Mar 2025 trading statement, with the GBR app concern, fell 13.2%. The DfT U-turn in Dec 2023 sent the stock up sharply. On 9 Oct 2026, the day the draft code came out, it rose 3.8%, so the market read the draft itself as benign.
findings.original_quote: Trainline believes that the proposed Code and frameworks require further strengthening to deliver fully on this commitment... Trainline will provide a fuller update on the regulatory landscape and its implications alongside its H1 FY2027 results on 4 November.
findings.why_not_priced: The market rallied 3.8% on the draft and +10.9% over 20 days, which prices the code as a relief. The 'implications' are by definition not yet disclosed. If the market already held a cautious read, the 9 Oct reaction and the 20-day run-up would not both be positive.
findings.independence: Partly shares the reset mechanism of finding 2, but rests on a different document (the regulatory commitment, not the CEO change). ORR's own release https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/trainline--trn/orr-proposals-for-rail-ticket-market-safeguards/9814463 confirms the code governs GBR's own retailer with a final code in spring 2027.

findings.finding: These are the first results under the new CEO, Ian Brown (in post 28 Sep). Sell-side FY28 consensus, updated 2 Nov, assumes a return to growth (NTS +4.0%, UK Consumer revenue +2.0%, EBITDA +2.7%), while the company says the UK headwinds (TOC self-preferencing, Project Oval) 'are expected to continue in the second half' after H1 UK Consumer revenue fell 5%. That is the setup for a new CEO to rebase the medium term or announce reinvestment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance and outlook lines move this name a lot: Sep 2025 TS +12.2%, Mar 2025 TS -13.2%, May 2025 finals -4.0% then -7.1%. The 24 Jun 2026 CEO appointment day itself was +0.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus updated on 2 Nov still carries FY28 growth on every line, and the stock is +10.9% over 20 days into the print. If a rebase were expected, FY28 numbers would have been cut toward FY27 and the run-up would not exist. This is an inference from the setup, not a disclosed number, so it is sized small against its range.
findings.independence: The headwind language comes from a different document, the company's 11 Sep TS: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/trainline--trn/trading-statement-and-notice-of-half-year-results/9766666. The CEO start date comes from https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/trainline--trn/directorate-change/9633069.
